articleTitle: Electrical Conductivity Control of Stretchable Printed Wires for In-mold Electronics Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Variations in electrical resistivity of stretchable wires printed with a silver-containing conductive paste consisting of a polyurethane binder on a glycol-modified polyethylene terephthalate (PETG) substrate were measured in situ during a vacuum-forming process to obtain a three-dimensional (3D) wire shape. When conductive paste containing silver flakes was used for the wire, the electrical resistivity was significantly reduced due to the stretching deformation during the forming process. It was also found that modifying the binder with a cross-linking agent effectively suppressed the electrical resistivity fluctuations of the 3D-shaped wires. The results of this study suggest that the conductivity of wires can be improved by controlling the material design and molding conditions. In addition, the wires bonded with chip LEDs using an electrically conductive adhesive were successfully integrally formed in a 3D shape by this process.

articleTitle: Realization of sub-4 µm Laser Microvia on ABF
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In recent years, high-density I/O has been implemented in IC packages. As a result, the density of wiring and drilling on build-up boards has significantly increased. A major bottleneck in achieving even higher density pattern on build-up boards is micro-vias formation. Thus, further miniaturization of microvias is one of the most important issues in packaging. We are developing a deep ultraviolet (DUV) laser processing machine that delivers intense laser pulses with a wavelength more than 30 times shorter than that of the CO2 lasers currently used for microvias processing. In this article, we demonstrate the drilling of sub-4 µm microvias on the Ajinomoto Build-up Film® (ABF) using direct DUV-laser processing. The sub 4-µm holes allow for a hole density that is twice as high as that of the 6-µm holes we reported previously.

articleTitle: Fan-out Wafer-level Packaging Process Integration for Artificial Intelligence Real Dies
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP) is recommended as a promised packaging technique to integrate heterogeneous chips into a system for high-performance applications. In this report, we propose a chip-last FOWLP process to fabricate the system-in-package (SiP) architectures, including artificial intelligence (AI) and memory real dies. We demonstrate a high-functionality package that can interconnect multiple chips into one system. Such a small form factor package structure would introduce many obstacles such as coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch effects between different materials and intrinsic stress induced by thermal budget. In this study, the complex design layout of redistribution layer (RDL) routing and optimization of the manufacturing process has been successfully demonstrated. X-ray analysis reveals a void-free performance in the package module. Thermal cycling tests have been performed to confirm the thermal stability of Showa Denko's granule molding compound implemented in FOWLP. The huge intrinsic warpage of a single module can be modulated by a modified substrate to achieve a relatively low module warpage. The package module was flip-chip bonded to the HDI board and assembled to a functional substrate to demonstrate the functionality of AI and memory dies.

articleTitle: X-Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) Investigations to Monitor the Cleanliness of Copper Surfaces During Palladium-Free Colloidal Copper Activation
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Palladium-free activators based on colloidal copper systems are proving to be robust alternatives to conventional ionic-palladium-based systems. Recent developments have shown that such colloidal copper activators can be used for electroless copper plating on a wide range of materials, including semi-additive process (SAP) relevant substrates, with plating performance competing with that of ionic palladium. Most promisingly, electrical reliability tests are shown to be free of interconnect defects (ICDs) providing evidence of good copper cleanliness after activation. These encouraging results fuel efforts to establish a detailed understanding of the surface chemistries for the full colloidal copper activation process with particular attention to the copper interconnects within through holes (TH) and capture pads within blind micro vias (BMVs). In this regard we have performed sequential X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis to monitor the surface chemistry of each step, from the conditioning to the deposition of the colloidal copper system (i.e. conditioner, acid rinse, selector, activation). Here we have chosen copper coated silicon wafers as a clean and practical substrate to represent copper surfaces. We monitored the N 1s spectra to determine the functionality and concentration of various organic components at the surface after each treatment step. Furthermore, we used the Cu Auger spectra to track the changes in the copper oxidation state. These XPS results qualitatively reveal significant insights into the role of the different treatment chemistries and how they influence cleanliness of copper surfaces. Interestingly we found that the acid rinse treatment shows good performance in removing the conditioner chemistry from the copper, whilst the selector treatment simultaneously exposes and stabilizes metallic copper at the surface. These XPS results thus reveal that the selector can minimize the amount of unfavorable oxide species. This detailed surface analysis using sequential XPS has provided valuable insights for the further developments of palladium-free colloidal copper activation processes. By understanding the specific roles of each treatment step and their impact on copper surfaces, we are now in a better position to optimize the entire process and can strive towards enhancing the reliability thereof.

articleTitle: Polymer Hybrid Bonding using Copper Paste and Photosensitive Adhesive for Copper-Copper Bonding at 200-250°C
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As the speeds of mobile communication systems continue to increase, demand is also rapidly increasing for semiconductor technologies that can transmit vast quantities of information at high speed with low latency. Solder bonding technology has traditionally been used for semiconductor chip mounting; however, owing to low reliability and difficulty in making connections below a 20-µm pitch by this method, alternative technologies are being developed. Recently, hybrid bonding has been developed as a copper-copper bonding technology that directly connects copper electrodes. However, hybrid copper-copper bonding, using inorganic materials in the insulation layer, requires a high degree of particle control and high temperatures of 300-400°C. This study introduces photosensitive adhesives and copper pastes for polymer hybrid bonding. Our photosensitive adhesives remain in a semi-cured state after patterning, and the copper paste can be sintered from 200°C, allowing copper-copper bonding to be performed at lower temperatures than conventional hybrid bonding while suppressing particle defects.

articleTitle: All-Solution-Processed Metallization of High Aspect Ratio Through Glass Vias (HAR-TGVs) with a High Adhesion Promoting Layer (APL)
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Metallization of through glass vias (TGV) by wet processing has received a lot of attention in recent years. However, there are two critical challenges - (i) the adhesion of the interface between the glass and the copper film is usually poor, (ii) void-free or seam-free filling of HAR-TGVs is challenging<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. In this study we developed a solution-based metal-oxide layer as the adhesion promoting layer (APL) which can be applied by various traditional coating approaches (Ex: spray coating, dip-coating and so on). The adhesion is around 6.5 N/cm, which is close to the commercial requirements<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-3</sup>. Adhesion is tested by using a 90-degree T-peel test. In the current work, our APL was deposited on the sidewall of the HAR-TGV using a ~109 nm-thick dip coat, as shown in Figure 1. We successfully demonstrate an all-solution-processed metallization and defect-free filling with APL for HAR-TGVs fabrication. The void-free HAR-TGVs filling can be achieved by using single-additive Cu filling formulation<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> under stagnant conditions, as shown in Figure 2. It is worth noting that the Cu bridge (butterfly pattern) can be formed under direct current (DC) and stagnant conditions unlike the complex periodic pulse reverse (PPR) plate waveform that is used in a complicated strong flow field environment, thereby offering a simple processing option.

articleTitle: Combining Process Modeling and Machine Learning Technology to Predict the Warpage of the Panel-Level Packaging After Debonding
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Fan-Out Panel-Level Packaging (FO-PLP) has emerged as a high-usage efficiency and cost-effective solution for advanced packaging. However, the challenge of excessive warpage significantly impacts its yield and reliability. To address this issue, this study focuses on analyzing the warping behavior using the Finite Element Method (FEM). Additionally, Process Modeling technology is employed in the simulations to enhance their realism and alignment with actual processes. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the factors contributing to the emergence of asymmetrical patterns in PLP. Various influential factors are taken into consideration, including geometrical uncertainty, material uncertainty, working platform inclination, and the influence of vacuum release paths. While simulations offer advantages in terms of time and cost, inconsistent results may arise due to variations in modelling approaches used by different researchers in finite element analysis. To overcome this challenge, the study proposes the utilization of artificial neural network (ANN) algorithms for warpage prediction in FO-PLP. The methodology involves constructing finite element models of different scales and establishing a training database based on these models. Subsequently, the ANN model is optimized by fine-tuning hyperparameters to obtain the most accurate predictive model. The proposed ANN model is expected to provide precise predictions of FO-PLP warpage in a shorter time compared to conventional simulations and experiments while ensuring reasonable accuracy. By harnessing the capabilities of machine learning, this study aims to overcome the limitations of traditional simulation methods and enhance the efficiency of FO-PLP warpage prediction. The findings of this research are anticipated to contribute to optimizing and improving the FO-PLP process, thereby enhancing the yield and reliability of advanced packaging applications.

articleTitle: Fitting Solder305 Anand Model Parameters with Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The Anand constitutive model is frequently utilized to explain the mechanical characteristics of solder materials in electronic components. In the Anand model, plasticity and creep are integrated and governed by a unified set of flow and evolutionary equations. The uniaxial tensile test results of Pb-free SAC305 are applied in this research to obtain the parameters of the Anand model. Due to the complexity of the model equations, it is difficult to determine all the parameters at once. The traditional approach involves using a standard multi-step procedure to estimate the model parameters. The experimental data used in this study were obtained from Motalab et al.[1], and the curve fitting method they employed was the least squares method. An artificial neural network (ANN) based method is applied for the parameter abstraction from the experimental results, with the freedom of initial guessing of these parameters. The framework and the procedure will be described. After completing the initial fitting of the Anand model, we will explore the influence of the specific parameters A, ho, and s<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> on the fitting of the model curve when they are varied across different orders of magnitude. Additionally, we will demonstrate the impact of Anand model with values at different orders of magnitude on the simulation results of finite element models for WLCSP (Wafer Level Chip Scale Packaging).

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Pig Size Detection in Smart Farm Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper presented the deep learning for pig size detection in farm imaging. The livestock industry in Taiwan is currently grappling with a critical shortage of manpower, necessitating prompt technological advancements. Compounded by the challenges of rural youth outmigration and declining birth rates, the industry faces a significant labor gap, resulting in reduced productivity. To address this issue, this study proposes the implementation of deep learning techniques in camera systems to enable real-time detection of pig sizes. By accurately assessing the condition of each pig, this innovative approach helps bridge the manpower shortage and enhances operational efficiency in the livestock sector, ultimately contributing to its sustainable growth.

articleTitle: Improvement of Adhesion between High-Frequency-Compatible Substrates with Low Dielectric Constants and Electroless Plated Copper Films Using a Vacuum Ultraviolet Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With the development of sophisticated and faster semiconductors, research is focusing on semiconductors that can work within high-frequency bands ranging from millimeter waves to sub-terahertz waves. To develop these semiconductors, the circuit substrates used for communication terminals and base stations should be capable of reducing signal attenuation or transmission loss, which increases at higher frequencies. Transmission loss is defined as the sum of dielectric loss and conductor loss. Dielectric losses can be reduced using a substrate material with a low dielectric constant (Dk) and a dielectric loss tangent (Df). Conductor losses are primarily due to the surface roughness and skin effect losses of its material at high frequencies. To reduce conductor losses, good adhesion should be achieved between the substrate and the conductor film without roughening the surface of the packaged substrate, i.e., the roughness at the interface between the wiring and the substrate should be low (Fig. 1). Cyclo olefin polymer (COP) is a suitable material for the next generation flexible substrates that allow high-speed transmission because of its dielectric properties. Vacuum ultraviolet (VUV, λ = 172 nm) excimer radiation with a photon energy large enough to break down organic matter can be used for the hydrophilization of polymer surfaces. Furthermore, under air atmosphere, the O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> can be photolyzed by absorbing a VUV light to generate reactive oxygen species such as O(1D), O(3P), and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. The reactive oxygen species that are produced can then initiate chemical reactions on the surface of materials being processed. (Fig. 2). This allows the formation of stronger interactions, which improve the adhesion between the surface and coating without the need for a conventional anchoring effect. [1], [2] In our previous study, [3], [4] we reported the surface modification of COP films by a VUV light, which resulted in an improvement of the adhesion strength between an electroless deposited copper and the COP substrate without roughening the surface. In this study, we analyzed the role of interface composition for achieving a good adhesion between the COP substrates and the deposited metal using a VUV-light irradiation without roughening their surfaces. Moreover, the mechanisms for achieving a strong adhesion between the substrates and electroless deposited copper by VUV-light irradiation were investigated.

articleTitle: Precise Warpage Control Technology for 12-Inch Bumpless Via-Last Chip-on-Wafer (COW) by Finite Element Method (FEM)
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: To realize the advanced information society, high-density and multi-layered structures such as Wafer-on-Wafer (WOW) and Chip-on-Wafer (COW) are required in the near future. This paper describes the influencing factors in reducing warpage during the resin molding process for COW, utilizing the Finite Element Method (FEM). It was confirmed that resin thickness significantly impacts warpage. To make a comparison, we replaced the base wafer material from silicon (Si) to glass with a higher coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) and simulated the results. Consequently, it was found that the warpage amount was reduced to one-sixth of the original value. Therefore, an effective approach to minimize wafer warpage is to reduce resin thickness as much as possible and then determine the required warpage amount through simulations, aiming to achieve the desired linear expansion of the substrate.

articleTitle: Novel Ultra-Low Dielectric Loss Tangent Resin with High Flame Retardancy for High-Frequency Printed Wiring Boards
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: To ensure high signal quality when operating in the high-frequency range, transmission losses must be reduced, and a low dielectric loss tangent is required for the insulating materials in printed wiring boards (PWBs). The dissipation factor of PWB materials for use in 5G base stations is at the 0.002-0.005 level, but post-5G and 6G equipment will require factors of 0.002 or even 0.001 or less. Olefins and other materials are being considered for use as next-generation low dielectric constant materials, but there is a trade-off between a low dielectric loss tangent and flame resistance for these materials, and no material that combines both properties has been reported to date. In this work, we have developed a novel material that offers both a low dielectric loss tangent and high flame retardance. This material has a dielectric loss tangent of less than 0.001, which is very low when compared with the PPE-based materials currently in use. Furthermore, the chemical structure has been optimized to provide flame resistance equivalent to that of the UL-94 V-0 standard. In addition, it also has thermosetting properties and a high glass transition temperature, which are required for PWB materials, and is expected to be a next-generation low dielectric loss tangent material.

articleTitle: AC Noise Enhancement with Fan-out Embedded Bride Package Solution
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: High-performance computing (HPC) and big data computing (BDC) play the most important role because it can perform calculations quickly and accurately, requiring billions or trillions of transistors to support the results. These HPC and BDC designs larger chip sizes and package sizes, resulting in very low yield and experience costs. What the electronics industry is doing is breaking down large chips into small chip-based devices to increase yields and reduce overall costs. Chiplet packaging has become a key technology for continuation of Moore's Law. Many package types were developed for this purpose including 2.5D, 3D, EMIB and Fan-out family. (FO-MCM, FO-EB and FO-EB-T). In this article, we will introduce FO- EB- T packaging technology (Fan-Out Embedded Bridge TSV). Based on package structure of view, the difference between FO- EB and FO- EB- T package is on embedded die structure. The benefit of FO- EB- T come from better electric performance (compared to FO-EB package) and lower package cost (compared to 2.5D package) better warpage control (compared to FO- MCM package). The paper will also demonstrate FO- EB- T package design (interconnection for SOC with HBM), simulation and measurement of electrical performance (reduce AC noise and power enhancement) and warpage mismatch.

Author Keywords: Fan-out embedded bridge Through Silicon Via (FO-EB-T)

articleTitle: Micro-Defect Failure Analysis in Fan-Out Package and Correspond to Finite Element Method (FEM) Simulation Results
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The Fan-Out (FO) structures are used for the heterogeneous integration packages recently because it offer high I/O counts, high-integration capability, thinner package and the lower cost. As the complexity of multiple chips packages increased continuously, the failure analysis (FA) workflow are constantly facing the new challenges. In this paper, we investigate the FO package with the open failed after the temperature cycle test (TCT). The FA workflow is examined by the electrical testing, the 3 Dimensions X-Ray Microscope (3D X-Ray) and the Focus Ion Beam (FIB) to find out the failure location and the defect mode. Finally, we use finite element method (FEM) to investigate the global and the local stress distribution.

articleTitle: Photosensitive Polyimides Compositions with Low Dielectric Property and Good Flexibility Corresponding to Redistribution Layers for Next Generation Heterogeneous Integration technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The demand for processing big data has increased due to digital transformation in various industries. This technical trend has been particularly pronounced in the past decade in connection with the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and 5G high-frequency connectivity. Accordingly, various electronic devices have been required to deliver higher performance year after year.

articleTitle: Ideal Flow Design of the Bending of Bi-Material Sheets
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The ideal flow theory is an efficient tool for the preliminary design of metal forming processes. The present paper applies this theory to design the bending of bi-material sheets. Generally, ideal flow solutions are not unique and additional criteria are needed to archive uniqueness. The proposed design ensures the sheet's desirable final inner and outer radii. The ideal flow condition determines the unique loading path that transforms the initial configuration into the final configuration.

articleTitle: PCB Solution with Partial Plane-on-Outer-Layer (POOL) Stackup
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: using partial POOL design can help move some high-speed signals from outer layer to inner layer for better performance without increasing PCB layer. However, the imbalanced copper density caused by partial POOL stackup may bring risks. This paper shares the work of risk evaluation. Potential failure modes are identified. Corresponding risks are evaluated through fabrication, reliability, assembly, SI tests on test boards.

articleTitle: Development of Raman Spectroscopy for Defect Analysis in SiC Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Recently, SiC has gained increasing popularity in high voltage power devices, since it can handle much higher breakdown voltages compared to traditional silicon-based devices. However, the defect density in SiC wafers remains high. In this report we explore the role Raman spectroscopy can play to identify different types of defects in SiC wafers and devices. We focus on two prominent bands: The peak 776 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> is related to local residual stress and can be used to identify basal plane dislocations (BPD). The peak at 970 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> is sensitive to the doping concentration and can be used to judge electrical uniformity of the SiC wafer without contact.

articleTitle: The effect and application of low VOC automatic cleaning process
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: No-clean flux has been widely used in electronic products like server, handheld…etc. because the non-cleaning process has the advantages of shortening the manufacture process. Due to high reliability requirements, automotive and medical products tend to implement cleaning process to remove flux residues and reduce the risk of electrochemical migration (ECM) and corrosion. In the past, PCBA used highly volatile organic solvents such as isopropanol (IPA) to remove flux residue and contaminant, which is not friendly to labor safety and environment. In contrast, the water-based cleaning agent has the characteristics of low VOC, no flash point and environment friendly. Therefore, the industry gradually uses water-based cleaning agents to clean PCBAs instead of organic solvent. In this paper, we demonstrate the cleaning result of an automatic cleaning machine using a water-based cleaning agent for high-end electronics and inspect the flux residues inside BGA component. The experimental results show that PCB board cleaning with 100% water pressure for 600 s, it can be clearly observed that the flux has been completely removed from the QFP leads and BGA solder joints. The surface cleanliness of the cleaned PCB board is tested by Resistivity of Solvent Extraction (ROSE, IPC-TM-650 2.3.25), and it can be seen that the surface cleanliness is 0.51µg NaCl/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. By using water-based cleaning agents, the VOC emission has reduced significantly from the 780 g/L (IPA) to 20 g/L (water-based cleaning agents).

articleTitle: High-speed Channel Design and Correlation Between Signal Integrity and Electrical Validation of Datacenter Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: As the data center industry grows rapidly and high-speed signal data rate increases, the channel design and electrical characterization are crucial to ensure the quality of the high-speed signal. Correlation of high-speed input/output (HSIO) channel design and its electrical characterization are crucial to help the silicon and platform designer to understand how the system channel design would affects the silicon HSIO physical (PHY) layer's receiver (RX) equalizer functions in optimizing the high-speed signal data transmission with low bit error rate (BER). This paper provides a comprehensive correlations of Signal Integrity (SI) measurement and Electrical Validation (EV) data collected on various Intel based datacenter platforms.

articleTitle: Solution Insight of Platform Printed Circuit Board Fiber-Wave Resonance Beyond 28 GHz High Speed SerDes Application
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Fiber-wave resonance effect with normal fiber pitch 500 μm significantly damages insertion loss when SerDes Nyquist frequency is beyond 28GHz, and potential solutions are desired for platform designers in further generation product development. The industry's well-known methods for PCI-E Gen 4, PCI-E Gen 5, PCI-E Gen 6, etc. applications, such as 10-degree trace routing orientation or normal spread fiberglass to address fiber-wave propagation delay skew nowadays becomes helpless for fiber-wave loss-resonance effect in higher data rate application such as PCI-E Gen 7 with 128 GT/s. This paper proposes analytical equations to predict the fiber-wave resonant frequency depending on selections of printed circuit board (PCB) material, the style of fiberglass fabric, core and prepreg construction, etc. On the other hand, test vehicles had been designed and measured to correlate simulation prediction. The proposed analytical method enables the possibility of promoting further generation PCB solutions from ecosystem advanced technology development perspective as well as the insight of what the market needs from the platform designer point of view.

articleTitle: A New Flex Electroless Nickel Chemistry for Flex ENIG and ENEPIG Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Flexible electroless nickel immersion gold (Flex ENIG) processes have been widely utilized for over two decades in flexible PCB fabrication with little modification or upgrade. With increasing demand for flexible electronics, miniaturization, and increasing popularity of the Internet of Things (IoT), flexible PCB fabrication continues to show growth coupled with increasing demand for technology advancement. At the heart of flexible ENIG is a specialized electroless nickel (EN) formulation that delivers a columnar structure, which produces a microcrack fracture mechanism upon bending. This eliminates the risk of crack propagation through to the underlying copper and the risk of open circuits. In this paper, we have demonstrated experimentally, as well as theoretically, how to promote and maintain a columnar EN structure, with contrast to the traditional electroless nickel deposit. Extensive EN structure analysis is supported with MIT bend test data to demonstrate an extraordinary electroless nickel working life, providing fabricators with significant operational benefits and waste savings. Continuing with the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) theme, further waste reductions are proven by elimination of dummy activation and compatibility demonstrated with both traditional cyanide and cyanide-free based immersion gold systems, with a focus on soldering and corrosion performance. As the trend towards miniaturization continually challenges fabrication processes, we evaluate the interactions between activation and electroless nickel chemistry to optimize this synergy, allowing for excellent fine line plating capability. Wirebonding has been another important aspect in recent times for Flex ENIG process. It is common to see Al instead of Au wirebonding for Flex ENIG surface finishes since nickel will diffuse into the gold wire and form a brittle Au-Ni intermetallic. In the case where gold wire is preferred, one way to address this issue is to increase the immersion gold thickness to minimize the nickel diffusion into gold wire. This can create excessive corrosion concerns due to the galvanic displacement nature of the immersion gold process and create another issue to manage. ENEPIG is well known to have reliable Al and Au wirebonding performance, due to the Pd interlayer providing a diffusion barrier. The new Flex EN is fully suitable for the ENEPIG process and a detailed study of Flex ENEPIG process will also be addressed.

articleTitle: PCI Express Receiver Channel Signal Quality Validation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This PCI Express Receiver Channel Signal Quality Validation Method is a new way to estimate the Receiver(RX) channel quality except for the traditional method which uses the Bit Error Rate Tester(BERT) to verify the Receiver(RX) channel quality by reaching the 1E-12 Bit Error Rate(BER). This method introduces a test fixture(Interposer board) to have a way to capture the compliance waveforms from device Transmitter(TX) side to CPU Receiver(RX) side. Then use the Sigtest Phoenix [4] tool which published by PCI-SIG to analyze the compliance waveforms and then get an accurate report from it. This method can give us a quick, reliable, and visible point of view to judge our receiver channel design quality. In other hand, it also can give us a direction to improve our receiver channel design.

articleTitle: A Study of Adhesion Enhancement for Porous Nickel Plating Treated Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: The growing utilization of semiconductor devices in the automotive industry and power device industry has underscored the critical importance of their reliability. Among the various methods available to enhance the reliability of semiconductor devices, improving the adhesion between epoxy molding compounds (EMC) and the lead frame (LF) stands out as a significant approach. This study explores how porous nickel plating enhances adhesion through two methods: the anchoring effect and chemical bonding. The diverse range of shapes and pore sizes in porous nickel plating offers a solution to adhesion challenges. Through a comparison of adhesion on nickel-plated and copper surfaces and an analysis of resin responses, this study reveals strategies for achieving optimized adhesion in semiconductor packaging, satisfying diverse application requirements.

articleTitle: Difference Frequency of EMI Shielding Solutions for SiP Module
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: More and more wireless connectivity device market refers to the industry that provides technologies and solutions for wireless communication between devices. This technologies including Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, 5G cellular networks, and other wireless communication standards such as Internet of Things (IoT) requirement for the rise of smart homes, smart cities, and industrial automation has increased the demand for wireless connectivity solutions that can support a wide range of devices and applications. Difference wireless connectivity which means difference frequency during air transmission from product to product. Even same product had control difference working frequency to get the better data rate transmission, so the EMI (Electromagnetic Interference) is an electrical phenomenon that happen when electromagnetic waves emitted from one device interfere to another device to cause the problems including signal degradation, data loss, and function failure. To meet the electrical EMI protection requirement, the advanced SiP could integrate difference solutions such as mulit-IC, passive components and antenna design into SiP module with EMI shielding solutions to get small form factor and good EMI protection. In this paper, we proceed a test vehicle which is designed to study the difference working frequency and verify the shielding effectiveness (SE) performance by near field scan inside the shielding room. The different frequency for EMI shielding solution and study difference EMI material for to measure under frequency of KHz to GHz frequency range. Difference material for EMI shield for shielding SE perofmrance comparison and use simulation program was used to evaluate the effectiveness of EMI shielding performance. Finally, this paper will demonstrate the advanced SiP with difference EMI shielding solutions for future RF, 5G connectivity devices application.

articleTitle: Low Temperature Double Pulse Test Platform for Testing Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Parasitic inductance and temperature are critical factors in power module design, impacting switching stability and system integrity. This study presents a novel double pulse test platform capable of assessing power module switching behavior under high current (>1000A) and low temperature (-40°C) conditions. The platform facilitates the evaluation of parasitic parameter effects on power module and DESAT protection designs in the gate driver board. Notably, our work demonstrates the occurrence of self-sustained oscillation effects during the turn-on transient of the low-side transistor, contrasting the traditional turn-off transient. Experimental results showcase the successful operation of the designed platform and gate driver board, enabling comprehensive switching assessments at 1100A and -40°C. This study provides valuable insights to designers, assisting in mitigating unintended phenomena during switching transients in practical systems.

articleTitle: An Effective Uniformity Improvement For Fan-Out Panel Level Packaging Electroplating
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In the packaging industry, Fan-out Panel Level Packaging (FOPLP) is considered advanced technology. It can achieve heterogeneous integration platform and reduce cost though extending utilization area of larger manufacturing format Electroplating (ECP) copper in redistribution layer (RDL) plays an important role of FOPLP system that it determines the electrical and mechanical properties of packaging structure. However, RDL thickness uniformity control in large system is very difficult. Furthermore, product with similar plating open ratio only suitable in the same shielding/sharing parts, these limit the utilization area of FOPLP product The study provide an efficient solution via optimal ECP shielding/sharing parts determination and well-designed modulating pattern that not only improve RDL thickness uniformity from below 80% to nearly 90% but also provide a universality ECP hardware suit for 17-66% plating open ratio which cover each product.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Thermal cycle and Drop Shock Reliability at Board Level with Developed Solder Composition by Optimized Bi, Cu, Ni Contents in Lead Free Solder Composition
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: We did study for development of new solder composition to cover the positive reliability of SAC305 as high thermal shock and SAC1205N as high drop shock reliability. However, general Sn-Ag-Cu solder composition have limitation of stable material property in thermal affecting condition because solder hardness is easily changed by microstructure due to merging of Ag3Sn particles which makes decreasing of precipitation hardening mechanism [1]. So, Sn-Ag-Cu-Ni-Bi solder has broadly studying at IDMs, OSATs and universities for application of FOWLP, FCBGA, SiP and DSP [2]–[7]. However, it must show lower drop shock reliability than SAC1205N solder composition due to high brittle property. The material hardness of new solder composition is controlled by substitutional hardening mechanism by Bi element instead of precipitation hardening in Sn based solder composition. The high contents of Bi in SNC (Sn-0.065Ni-0.75Cu) makes the high brittle property compare to non-Bi solder composition. However, we find that optimum Bi contents in SNC composition as below 2wt%. The 3wt% Bi solder also has reasonable ductile property at fractured area after tensile test. However, brittle fracture was seriously increased over Bi 5 wt% in SNC solder composition due to Bi segregation by excessive Bi element which is high brittle property as rhombohedral structure [8]. So, we find that when Bi contents is the 1.5 to 2.0 wt% in SNC solder (JY T2), that compositions can overcome the higher thermal shock reliability than SAC305 and higher drop reliability than SAC1205N solder composition. Even 3wt% Bi in SNC solder (JY T4) had lower elongation property than SAC305, it shown higher drop shock reliability because Ni additive makes more stable interfacial IMC layer than that of SAC305 after drop shock test. Our developed solder composition called JY T2(1.5Bi) and JYT4(3.0Bi) The optimized Bi content in JY solder composition shown higher drop than SAC1205N about 2 times on Cu OSP pad finish. And also, Thermal shock reliability of optimized Bi contents solder shown higher than SAC305 solder composition around 2 times on Cu-OSP pad finish. Therefore, the optimized Bi in JY composition can be replace of all lead-free solder composition because it shown satisfaction of drop and thermal shock reliability.

articleTitle: Noise Analysis and Improvement of Power Supply Network Based on Power Integrity
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Power supply integrity is very important in digital systems. When the frequency on the power loop becomes higher, the impedance on the loop will gradually increase. The change in voltage drop will also cause the fluctuation of the output voltage to increase, and eventually causing the overall system becomes unstable and loses efficiency. The coupling capacitance on the loop plays an important role for these phenomenon. In this paper, the output voltage of the switching power supply is supplied to the microcontroller for operation. Simulation software is used to analyze the impedance on the power loop, and the circuit board is used to implement the method of operation and measurement will be discussed in depth on their principles and characteristics.

articleTitle: A new x-ray source technology for demanding SMT and Semiconductor inspection (IMPACT 23, S20-3)
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: This source is based on advanced electron optics and the latest very thin tungsten- diamond transmission target technology. Automatic e-beam focusing, and astigmatism correction ensures that the smallest possible, truly round focal spot is achieved. The NanoTube also has the unique feature of internally measuring and reporting the current spot size. In addition, advanced cooling, and cutting-edge thermal design results in extreme stability over time. This enables an unprecedented true resolution of 150nm lines and spaces. The true round spot of the tube is demonstrated by the highly symmetric images of a ‘Siemens star’ resolution target, the innermost features are 150 nm. The NanoTube is the focus of this paper and work is currently on going, Excillum have already purchased a leading high-end manufacturers off-line system which has become our ‘real life’ test bed, so far, we have benchmarked the source and have upgraded it to the highest current industry specification. We have now replaced the source with the recently developed Excillum NanoTube, running at higher power, offering all the advantages listed, plus further improved electron optics, reliability, and redesigned exterior for easier installation into existing cabinets. The paper will contain comparison data and images from the current industry best vs. the latest Nano Focus tube, plus data from reliability and stability tests using a real-life system and not test rigs. Key words; x-ray, electronics inspection, Lab6, Nano tube, FOD, radiation damage, flux density, open transmissive.

articleTitle: Smart Electroless Copper Bath for SAP Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Several electroless copper bath features such as bath stability, copper deposit color and crystal structure, throwing power and suppression of nanovoiding, are decisive in determining the suitability thereof for a particular application, but the deposited copper thickness and the copper deposition speed are particularly important in deciding which bath is the right one for the task at hand. Especially for fine line-and-space applications, the demand for a very thin and uniform copper layer is becoming ever more important. The main challenge for an electroless copper bath depositing ultra-thin layers is to reach the desired thickness in typical dwell times of around 15 - 20 minutes. In this report, the results of a study carried out to investigate the plating behavior of an electroless copper bath specifically tailored for the deposition of ultra-thin electroless copper layers are presented. The surface-active additive therein is particularly crucial in directing the copper deposition speed and determining the final electroless copper thickness. This bath does not only deposit without any need for dummy plating, it could also be shown that it sustains plating until a smooth and uniform electroless copper layer is achieved, regardless of the substrate and its roughness. This behavior can be considered as smart, since the bath “knows” when the time has come to suppress deposition.

articleTitle: All-GaN HEMTs and Planar Transformer Based 48V Voltage Regulator Common Module (VRCM) Design
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: An all GaN (Gallium Nitride) HEMTs (High Electron Mobility Transistors) based 48V to 12V Voltage Regulator Common Module (VRCM) is proposed in this paper for datacenter 48V rack. articleTitle: Low Contact Resistance and Low Temperature Hybrid Bonding with Polyimide and Highly <111>-oriented Nanotwinned Cu
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: Among the recent decades, the development of fine pitch hybrid bonding is eye-catching, since this kind of technology could realize high-speed signal transmission with high reliability due to the shrunk electrical joints and the surrounded dielectrics [1]. The polyimide (PI) possesses low Dk (~3.61 at IMHz), low Df (~0.037 at 1MHz), low curing temperature, simple process ability at low cost, excellent mechanical properties, high resistance and stability. It is considered as an excellent candidate to protect joints and enhance their bonding strength [2]. As for nanotwinned copper (NT-Cu), it is also a candidate for low-temperature Cu-Cu bonding. Highly <111>-oriented NT-Cu can be electroplated with good uniformity on Si wafers. With the high surface diffusivity and the low oxidation rate [3]–[4], the bonding can be achieved at lower temperature in the same time. The bonding temperature can be reduced to below 250 °C by using high surface diffusivity NT-Cu and low curing temperature PI which has low glass transition temperature (Tg), and increase the bonding strength simultaneously. As a result, PI is incorporated with highly <111>-oriented nanotwinned Cu (NT-Cu) to achieve the low contact resistance hybrid bonding (< 1.7 x 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> Ω. cm2) with low bonding temperature (220 °C) in this study.

articleTitle: A Precision Enhancement Deep Learning Framework for Package Substrate Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: In the manufacturing industry, producing a large quantity of highquality products every day is the top priority. Recently, the integration of Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) equipment and Deep Neural Network (DNN) defect image predictions has demonstrated a significant reduction in manual effort required for defect inspection in manufacturing industrial applications. However, during substrate manufacturing, changes in in-process conditions can lead to unexpected variations in defects, such as combinations of multiple defects or anomalies that humans are not familiar with. Consequently, mainstream DNN-based object detection (OD) methods have yet to achieve the desired accuracy for detecting these defects images in production line, and hence human visual inspections remain essential. In this paper, we propose a defect detection framework to both reduce the need for human examination and maintain the high quality of normal products for downstream processes. This method integrates three DNN methods: OD, anomaly detection (AD), and auxiliary classification (AC). OD constructs hyperplanes for bounding-box objects and classes. AD measures distances between embedding vectors trained from normal samples to detect anomalies. AC operates by centering the object proposed by OD within a cropped image and re-judging the object's class, which can refine OD's anchor-based training. We conducted an ASE manufacturing dataset experiment, and our method reduced human examination by 28%, with only a 2.8% underkill rate. Combining OD and AC achieved 93.21% defect classification accuracy, surpassing mainstream accuracy 89.74%. With the assistance of our new framework, we are able to simultaneously reduce the manual efforts for examination and increase the accuracy of defect classification. When applied in MFG production lines, this technology can surely assist our factory operation, enabling us to better meet a smart factory requirements.

articleTitle: Simulation Modeling of 600mm X600mm Fan-Out Panel Level for Warpage Behavior Based on Chip First
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)

articleTitle: Printed Circuit Board (PCB) Design Electrical Characterization and Optimization in Immersion Cooling Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 18th International Microsystems, Packaging, Assembly and Circuits Technology Conference (IMPACT)
abstract: With data centers' power consumption continuing to increase in recent years, immersion cooling is gaining significant traction and emerging in many scenarios to improve cooling efficiency [1]. Electrical characterization of information technology (IT) components may be affected from air cooling condition to immersion cooling condition. This paper focuses on immersion cooling impact on PCB, especially microstrip line through modeling, simulation, and measurement.
